text:
Olivia: FYI — canary pool in us-central1 started failing after driver 550.3 rollout. DKMS builds are erroring with unresolved linker symbols (e.g. nv_kref_put). Affected hosts boot but pods using CUDA images go CrashLoopBackOff.

deploy-bot: canary-rollout(550.3) -> FAILED on 4/10 hosts. rollout paused.

Rafael: Can you paste dkms build output? My hunch is kernel header symlink or GCC mismatch. Try:
```
$ dkms build -m nvidia -v 550.3
...
modpost: Found 1 unresolved symbol: nv_kref_put
ERROR: modpost failed
```

Tanya: I'm seeing two different kernels across the failing nodes: 6.3.8 vs 6.1.12. Also /lib/modules/6.3.8/build is a broken symlink on host-7. `ls -l /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build` -> 'No such file or directory'

Olivia: Also noticed GCC mismatch: some nodes have gcc-12, others gcc-11. DKMS uses host gcc to build kernel modules.

Sam: This looks like an image bake drift — packer recipe didn't pin linux-headers. ap-southeast images are pinned, which is why they are fine.

infra-ci: Reproduced in a test VM: `dkms install -m nvidia -v 550.3` fails with 'Cannot find suitable kernel source tree' and later 'modpost: unresolved symbol'.

Rafael: Mitigation: pause rollout (done), revert canary to 549.1, and add a preflight that verifies:
- /usr/src/linux-headers-$(uname -r) exists
- gcc --version matches expected (12)
- dkms build passes

Tanya: I'll push a hotfix to the image bake to pin linux-headers and add the preflight to our provisioning hooks (chef/packer). Opening a task for provider image drift report.

Olivia: Assigning: Tanya (bake hotfix), Rafael (rollback + validation), Sam (capacity choreography). ETA 2h? We need to avoid overloading other regions due to quota/cost.

Rafael: Rollback started. Draining canary nodes and redeploying 549.1 kernel + driver. Monitoring health.

deploy-bot: rollback-complete: canary reverted to 549.1. All 4 failing hosts back to healthy.

Sam: Quick cost note — shifting running jobs to us-east will cost extra egress and instance price. Flagged to finance.

Olivia: Please add a short postmortem and include kernel-header alignment and preflight checks. Thanks :pray:
